chunks: And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When Allah loves a servant, He safeguards him, places his richness within his soul, and places his reward before his eyes. And when He despises him, He leaves him to his own soul, and places his poverty before his eyes.

key_terms.بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ: Before his eyes (metaphor for constant visibility/accessibility)
key_terms.عَصَمَهُ: He safeguards him (from sin and error)
key_terms.وَكَلَهُ إِلَى نَفْسِهِ: He left him to his own soul (to his own devices)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the spiritual state of those Allah loves and those He despises?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine mechanism of *'ismah* (guardianship) and self-sufficiency, where Allah's love manifests as inner richness and the tangible presence of reward, while His displeasure results in abandonment to one's own ego. This hadith highlights the Shia concept that true wealth is spiritual contentment derived from divine proximity, contrasting it with the existential poverty of those left to their own devices. It underscores the transformative power of divine love in shaping the believer's internal state and perception of their deeds.
